request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"knewton::edtech","name":"knewton","one_liner":"Adaptive learning platform that licensed AI-powered personalization to publishers and universities, acquired by Wiley in 2019 for under $17M after raising ~$157M.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":3,"rationale":"Knewton was a B2B SaaS platform monetized via recurring enterprise subscriptions sold to publishers and universities. The new pitch is a direct-to-consumer tiered freemium app targeting K-12 students. Both involve subscription-style recurring revenue and adaptive/AI tutoring, but the go-to-market orientation (enterprise licensing vs. consumer freemium) diverges sharply."},"market":{"score":4,"rationale":"Both operate in the adaptive/AI-assisted learning space and share the core thesis that personalised instruction improves outcomes. However Knewton focused on US higher education and test-prep, while the new pitch targets K-12 consumers in Indonesia and the Philippines — different geographies, different age segments, and different buyer personas."},"gtm":{"score":2,"rationale":"Knewton sold through institutional partners (Pearson, Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, Arizona State University) as a white-label B2B platform. The new pitch goes direct-to-consumer with an app and a freemium funnel, a fundamentally different acquisition and conversion motion."},"stage_scale":{"score":4,"rationale":"Both are early-to-mid stage edtech ventures betting heavily on adaptive AI before achieving sustainable unit economics. Knewton raised large VC rounds across many years; the new pitch is presumably pre-revenue or early-revenue, so scale trajectories differ but the over-capitalisation risk is shared."}},"why_similar":"Both Knewton and the new pitch are built on the thesis that AI-driven adaptive learning can personalise education at scale. Knewton deployed real-time analysis of student performance data to make custom recommendations — exactly the core value proposition of the new pitch's AI tutoring layer. Both also incorporate a small-group or blended-learning element (Knewton's Arizona State deployment used blended learning courses alongside the adaptive platform). The shared failure mode of over-investing in technology infrastructure before locking in sustainable, repeatable revenue is directly relevant.","where_diverged":"Several concrete dimensions separate the two: (1) Geography — Knewton was US-headquartered and US-market-first; the new pitch targets Indonesia and the Philippines. (2) Customer type — Knewton's paying customers were enterprise institutions (publishers, universities); the new pitch's paying customers are individual consumers or families. (3) Business model — Knewton used B2B recurring subscription licensing; the new pitch uses a tiered freemium consumer model with a free tier that must convert to paid. (4) Target segment — Knewton focused on higher education and test-prep; the new pitch addresses K-12. (5) Pedagogy delivery — the new pitch explicitly pairs AI tutoring with weekly small-group human sessions, creating a blended human-AI product; Knewton was purely a technology API/platform layer.","failure_causes":["enterprise dependency on large publisher/institution partnerships","prolonged unprofitable growth on ~$157M raised before acquisition","inability to build a direct consumer or independent revenue stream","massive write-down at acquisition (raised >$157M, sold for <$17M)","product pivot away from core B2B API toward direct courseware without proven demand","slow sales cycles and high integration costs with institutional partners","commoditisation of adaptive learning as major publishers built in-house capabilities"],"lessons_for_input":["Validate willingness-to-pay among Indonesian and Filipino families before scaling AI infrastructure — Knewton never built a reliable direct-revenue channel and it proved fatal.","Keep the freemium conversion funnel extremely tight; a wide free tier with no clear upgrade trigger is a cash drain that burned edtech platforms relying on volume to justify valuations.","Avoid over-dependence on a single channel or partner type — Knewton's reliance on Pearson and other publishers left it exposed when those partners deprioritised the relationship.","The weekly small-group session is a meaningful product differentiator from pure-tech adaptive platforms; protect and operationalise it early as a retention and monetisation hook rather than treating it as a nice-to-have.","Raise only what unit economics justify — Knewton's $157M+ raise set an expectation of scale that the underlying B2B model could never meet; right-size capital to the Southeast Asian consumer market's actual ARPU."]}
